reply.thought: The handoff claims the refunds were applied, but I should verify against the ledger before paying anyone. I'll start by listing the refunds.
The ledger's refunds match the batch exactly: orders 130, 133, and 134 with the signed amounts. Next I'll list the orders so I know which customers to pay.
The ledger's refunds match the batch and the handoff, so I can proceed. Orders map to three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 28879 matches the order total (17595 + 26245) minus its refunds (8178 + 6783), so I'll record that payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance from the ledger rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net of 61735 matches its orders (37666 + 33067 = 70733) minus the order 134 refund (8998), so I'll record that payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance from the ledger rather than computing it myself.
Cobalt's orders total 10547 + 6294 = 16841 with no refunds against them, which matches the ledger's net of 16841. I'll record that payout.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matched the order totals minus the verified refunds, and every record_payout returned ok. The batch is complete.
